title: Breitspur 01
subtitle: 1972 BMW 2002
summary: Round tails, riveted Turbo flares, multipiece mesh wheels and a pink tow strap for Ruxin.
thesis: Breitspur's first concept car: a 1972 BMW 2002 drawn as the Turbo prototype that never was.  Round taillights and kidney grilles untouched, riveted flares, multipiece mesh wheels and a cage, and a set of quiet tributes to a small, fast dog named Ruxin.

photo.alt: Close detail of the 2002's front corner: riveted fender flare, polished mesh wheel, black grille and raw aluminum splitter with tow strap

parts.name: Black Anodized Early Grilles
parts.note: The all black side grilles in the render, made from the early aluminum grilles your car already has.  Have an anodizing shop strip them and anodize them black, so the color is part of the metal and cannot peel.  Ask for electrolytic (two step) black, which holds up in the sun better than dyed black, and a sealed finish.  Expect a satin result.  Take the plastic reflectors and hardware off first, and have the shop look them over before you commit.  Want to keep your originals?  Anodize a new set instead.
parts.priceNote: Anodizing is a local shop quote.  New early grille set with kidney, $1,250, linked here

also.label: 1974 or later car? Black plastic grilles bolt on, Mecatechnic

parts.name: Ground Control Complete Suspension
parts.note: Koni adjustable inserts, threaded perches and camber plates.  You send Ground Control your bare strut housings and they build on them.  Owners run this kit at zero fender gap, the height in these renders, and still drive their cars.  Set final height with your wheels and flares fitted, so the tires clear the arches under compression.

also.label: Budget path: Bilstein Sport struts and shocks, $702
Pair with H&R Sport springs, 1.25 in drop, $339.99
See owner cars on Ground Control, 2002FAQ forum

parts.name: Turbo Style Fender Flares
parts.note: Set of four in black ABS, shaped after the 2002 Turbo. Trim the arch lip, then rivet them on for the look in the render.

parts.name: BBS RS Three Piece, Staggered
parts.note: The riveted mesh wheel in the renders.  BBS RS centers came in 4 x 100 for the E30, and new 15 inch step lips and inner barrels let a builder set any width and offset.  Spec it staggered: 15 x 7 at about ET10 to ET15 in front, 15 x 8 at about ET0 in back.  Run 205/50R15 front and 225/45R15 rear; the two are within half a percent in diameter.  Test fit one wheel with the flares on and the car at ride height before the set is built.
parts.priceNote: A restored 15 x 7 set lists at $5,000.  A staggered build is quoted to order

also.label: Building it yourself? New 15 in RS step lips, WheelFlip, $227 each
Budget path: Rota RB 15 x 7 mesh, same size all round, about $1,000

parts.name: Front Air Dam plus Splitter Blade
parts.note: Ireland Engineering's flexible air dam is the base. The blade is yours to make: about 60 in of 1/8 in 5052 aluminum from a local metal supplier, cut to shape and riveted underneath.  At this ride height the blade is the lowest point on the car, so bolt or rivet it on as a replaceable part and expect to scrape it on steep driveways.

parts.name: Supersprint Muffler, Dual 60 mm Tips
parts.note: Rear muffler with twin tips, listed for the 1602, 2002 and 2002tii. Gives the M10 a real voice without drone.

parts.name: Sparco 6 Point Bolt In Cage
parts.note: FIA homologated steel cage with door bars, bolt in for 1968 to 1975 cars.  The seller has not confirmed fit, so match Sparco part 00723185 to your car before ordering.  Made to order, about nine weeks.

bundle.name: Stance Kit
bundle.pitch: The three parts that make this look, in install order: get it low, give it room, fill the arches.

detailing.note: Wash, then clay. Fifty year old single stage paint holds grime the mitt leaves behind.
Black single stage paint shows every swirl. A gentle polish brings back the depth. Expect black on the pad; that is the paint, and it is normal.
Spray on, wipe off. Ten minutes for months of gloss and water beading.

designerNote: Car companies build these raw, emotional things that never get to see the streets.  I want people to actually get to experience them.

conceptNote: The Breitspur 01 is a concept render, not a finished car.  Every part below is a real, off the shelf part, listed in install order, so you can build the attainable version of this look yourself.
deck: Breitspur's first concept car is a BMW 2002 that hits harder than it looks, and it is a tribute to a small, fast dog named Ruxin.  We talked with Nick DiLoreto, design director and principal of Breitspur, about what went into it.

article.label: The brief
article.heading: What was off limits when you started sketching?
body: The car is extremely iconic, so the round taillights and the kidney grilles were never up for discussion.  What I wanted was a beefier take on it.  A true tribute, something that could have been the prototype for the 2002 Turbo.
article.caption: Side profile.  The shape is untouched; everything sits lower and wider.

article.label: The tribute
article.heading: Who is Ruxin, and where does he show up in the car?
body: This build was a creative outlet for me after my dog Ruxin died, and the whole car is a tribute to him.  The tow straps are pink, not red, because they're meant to look like his little pink tongue.  He was a black dog with white on him, so the black, silver, and white palette comes from him.

He loved the ocean and the beach and anything with water, and that's the blue in the door cards.  He was also a very athletic little dog, always the fastest one at the dog park.  Small and fast, just like the car.
article.caption: Pink, not red.  The tow straps are for Ruxin.

article.label: The stance
article.heading: How do you make a 2002 look muscular without losing what makes it delicate?
body: Mostly with the flared arches and the multipiece wheels.  They give it that wide, low character I was after.  The centered rear exhaust makes the car look wider too, and it plays off the round taillights.
article.caption: Riveted flare, multipiece mesh wheel and the raw aluminum splitter.

article.label: The why
article.heading: Where does the urge to build something this raw come from?
body: When I was a young designer at Volvo I got to drive a prototype S40 they never did anything with.  It was raw, loud, and had loads of power, a monster.  I always found it a bit sad that car companies build these raw, emotional machines and the public never gets to see them.

I know a car that loud probably would have struggled with mass buyers, but there was something so cool about it.  For me, a huge part of all this is building those kinds of cars and letting people actually experience them.  That's what I tried to get across with the 01.
article.caption: Round tails, Turbo flares and the cage through the glass.

article.label: The driver
article.heading: Who is the 01 for?
body: It's a weekend car, not a daily driver.  It's stiff, it's loud, it's raw.  It's the thing you look forward to on Saturday morning, the car you grab when you want that adrenaline hit out on the backcountry roads.

article.label: The status
article.heading: Is it built?
body: Not yet, and I want to be upfront about that.  The 01 is our first concept car, and we hope to build it soon.

article.label: The last word
article.heading: What would Ruxin make of it?
body: He loved car rides.  When he was a puppy I had a Volkswagen GTI, and we'd take it to the park, the ocean, the lake.  There was nothing better than his face looking up at me from the passenger footwell, because he knew we were off to do something fun.  I think he'd connect this car with those same good things.
article.caption: Blue door cards, for a dog who loved the water.

article.label: Before you buy
article.heading: What we would tell a friend
body: Do not swap the nose to get black grilles.  Early cars, through August 1973, keep their own aluminum grilles; have them anodized black so the finish cannot peel.  The black plastic grilles bolt straight on only if your car is a 1974 or later.  The flares need the arch lip trimmed.  The cage listed here comes from Europe and runs about nine weeks, so order it first.
